what_its_for: Exemestane is used to treat breast cancer in women who have gone through menopause. It works by lowering the amount of estrogen (a female hormone) in your body, which helps slow or stop the growth of certain types of breast cancer cells that need estrogen to grow.
how_to_take: Take exemestane by mouth once a day, after a meal. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Taking it with food helps your body absorb the medicine better and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is one 25 mg tablet taken once a day after a meal. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store exemestane at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a safe medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking estrogen-containing products (such as hormone replacement therapy, estrogen creams, or birth control pills) while on exemestane, as they can make the medicine less effective. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it may increase the risk of bone loss and other side effects. Talk to your doctor before starting any new vitamins, supplements, or herbal products, especially St. John's Wort, as they may interfere with how this medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or swelling in your leg (possible signs of a blood clot); severe bone, joint, or muscle pain; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual vaginal bleeding; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; depression or significant mood changes; or if you fall and are concerned about a fracture. Also let your doctor know about any new or worsening side effects.
when_it_works: Exemestane starts working right away to lower estrogen levels in your body. However, it may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor can measure its full effect on your cancer. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel well. Breast cancer treatment is a long-term process, and stopping early can allow the cancer to return.
special_populations: Older adults: Exemestane is commonly used in postmenopausal women and is generally well tolerated, but bone loss (osteoporosis) is a greater concern. Your doctor may recommend calcium, vitamin D supplements, and regular bone density checks. Kidney or liver problems: If you have serious kidney or liver disease, tell your doctor, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Exemestane must NOT be used during pregnancy as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
